sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Strategic Objective**: The Marathas aimed to secure the 'North-Western Frontier' to prevent Afghan incursions led by Ahmad Shah Abdali.
• **Key Commanders**: The campaign was spearheaded by **Raghunath Rao** (Raghoba) and **Malhar Rao Holkar**.
• **Geopolitical Context**: The expulsion of **Timur Shah** (Abdali's son) from Lahore in 1758 marked the peak of Maratha influence in the Punjab.
• **Key Metric / Factor**: The expansion necessitated a massive logistical supply chain stretching from Pune to Attock, straining the Maratha treasury.

sections.title: Comprehensive Classification & Comparative Matrix
rows: Control over the Ganga-Yamuna Doab; collection of Chauth and Sardeshmukhi.
Need to buffer Delhi from Rohilla Afghan influence.
Prelims: Understanding the economic drain and administrative overreach.
Capture of Lahore (1758); reaching the Indus River; Adina Beg appointed as Governor.
Direct confrontation with Durrani interests; strategic depth.
Mains: Analysis of the 'Imperial Overstretch' theory.

items.definition: A shrewd local administrator in Punjab who played both sides (Marathas and Afghans) to maintain power; his appointment by Marathas was a tactical error due to his lack of loyalty.
The primary fiscal mechanisms used by Marathas to extract revenue from newly conquered territories in the North, often alienating local populations.

items.title: Major Applications / Initiatives
items.content:
• **Strategic Alliance**: Attempting to align with the Sikhs and Jats to create a unified front against Afghan invaders.
• **Frontier Defense**: Establishing military outposts as far as Attock to monitor the Khyber Pass.

items.title: Challenges & Way Forward
items.content:
• **Key Challenges**: Lack of local support in Punjab, over-reliance on distant supply lines, and the 'alien' nature of Maratha administration in the North.
• **Solutions**: Integration of local military elites (Sikhs/Jats) into the Maratha administrative fold.

items.title: Mnemonic for Retention
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym**: 'R-A-M' (Raghunath, Adina, Maratha).
• **Decoded Meaning**: Raghunath Rao led the campaign, Adina Beg was the local governor, and the Maratha flag flew at Attock.

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC often confuses the 'First Phase' (1752 treaty with Mughals) with the 'Second Phase' (1757-58 direct occupation). Ensure you distinguish between the 'Protector of the Mughal Throne' role and the 'Direct Occupier' role.
Mains Value Addition: Use the term 'Imperial Overstretch' when discussing why the Marathas failed to hold Punjab. It demonstrates an analytical understanding of military history.

keyTakeaways: The Maratha advance to the Indus was the furthest territorial expansion of the Maratha Empire.
The failure to consolidate Punjab directly invited Abdali's return, leading to the Third Battle of Panipat.
The reliance on local opportunists like Adina Beg proved fatal to Maratha stability in the North.
